# Incident Report — 2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.9.10.102** |
| MAC address | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** (domain `angrypoutine.com`, NetBIOS `ANGRYPOUTINE`) |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS exchanges between 10.9.10.102 and DC 10.9.10.9) |

## Malware Family
**IcedID (Bokbot)** — attribution is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed (no AV/YARA engine or internet threat-intel lookup was used, per instructions). Basis for the call:

- Classic IcedID "gate" pattern: HTTP GET to a nonsense multi-segment URI path (`/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?...`) using a spoofed outdated IE7 user-agent string, answered by a PHP/Apache server serving a `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"` payload that is actually a Windows PE32+ DLL (MZ header, x86-64) — the standard IcedID loader delivery mechanism.
- Immediately following the gate check-in, the host opens a TLS session direct-to-IP (no SNI extension sent) on port 443 to an unrelated host, presenting a **self-signed certificate** (CN `londonareloeli.uk`, O "LL EST", "UK System", Subject=Issuer). This is IcedID's known backconnect/C2 channel behavior.
- The identical self-signed certificate (same CN/serial pattern) reappears on a **second, independent C2 IP** used for sustained beaconing (30+ reconnects spanning the entire ~4600-second capture) — consistent with IcedID's multi-endpoint, persistent C2 model.

## Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints (IP:port)
| Endpoint | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **167.172.37.9:443** | TLS session immediately after the gate hit; self-signed cert CN `londonareloeli.uk`; 226 packets in / 83 out, 311 kB over 4.5s (frames ~1479–1550+), no SNI sent |
| **94.158.245.52:443** | Same self-signed cert CN `londonareloeli.uk`; persistent low-and-slow channel, 33 separate TCP handshakes to port 443 recurring from t=148s through t=4512s (full capture duration), no SNI sent |

### Malicious domain
| Domain | Resolved IP | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **simpsonsavingss.com** | 194.62.42.206 | DNS query at t=139.2s; HTTP GET follows at t=140.0s |

### Malicious URL
- `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS`
  - Full request/response captured in TCP stream 50. Server: `Apache/2.4.6 (CentOS) OpenSSL/1.0.2k-fips PHP/7.2.34`. Response headers: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Length: 284816`.

### Transferred file
| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Server-assigned filename | `date6` |
| File type | PE32+ executable (DLL), GUI subsystem, x86-64 |
| Size | 284,816 bytes |
| SHA256 | `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8` |
| Delivery | Downloaded via the URL above, immediately preceding the first C2 TLS handshake to 167.172.37.9 |

## Benign Context (ruled out, not IOCs)
Windows Update / Delivery Optimization (`download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`), Microsoft telemetry/NCSI (`www.msftncsi.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com`, `v10.events.data.microsoft.com`), Microsoft Store (`store-images.s-microsoft.com`, `storeedgefd.dsx.mp.microsoft.com`), Microsoft/Bing/Office/Teams/OneNote/Outlook edge services (`msedge.net` ring hosts, `nexus.officeapps.live.com`, `cdn.onenote.net`, `login.live.com`), Intel gameplay API, Google Update (`update.googleapis.com`), and `myexternalip.com` (a common but non-conclusive IP-check lookup, not tied to any observed malicious payload here).

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-KKITB6Q (10.9.10.102, MAC 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3), logged in as domain user `hobart.gunnarsson`, retrieved a PE32+ DLL payload from a fake-header HTTP GET to `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206) at approximately T+140s, consistent with an IcedID gate/loader delivery. Within four seconds the host established outbound TLS connections to two separate external IPs (167.172.37.9 and 94.158.245.52) on port 443, both presenting an identical self-signed certificate for `londonareloeli.uk` and neither providing an SNI value, indicating a hardcoded IcedID C2 backconnect. The second C2 channel persisted with repeated reconnects for the remainder of the capture (~75 minutes), indicating an active, ongoing infection at the time recording stopped.
